lastText: File ClosedThe Republic's Last AddressMajor DefeatItalian High Command, 1939–1945End of hostilities: APRIL 28, 1945 · filed with minor delayImmediate AftermathThe Italian Social Republic ends on April 28, 1945, twenty months after Mussolini's rescue from Gran Sasso installed it as a German client state in the occupied north. The human cost of this path runs higher than the historical one at nearly every hinge point: Italy's own wartime dead, roughly 300,000 military and civilian combined split across two governments and a country fought over twice, were already among the higher tolls of any Axis power relative to population. The armistice announcement was actually delayed long enough to concentrate a real defense around Rome: a stand the historical chaos of September 8-9, 1943 never gave the scattered garrison any chance to mount, even though the city still fell within the week regardless. Mussolini's answer to Romania was delayed rather than rushed: the single change every honest account of the Greek campaign says should have been made, and on this path, was. Graziani ordered the withdrawal from the fortified camps before Compass's flanking attack landed, rather than holding as the historical delay did: sparing the Tenth Army the worst of a rout that historically cost some 130,000 men taken prisoner.
